translationRepairs: Lunar eclipse yin-calendar limit: 4,300; fixing divisor 430.

s0015 gives 日食陽曆限 and s0016 continues with bare 陰曆限; s0017 separately introduces 月食限. The idiomatic 'Lunar eclipse' invents a lunar-eclipse reading the Chinese does not support; dropping that phrase restores the source.
For Mercury, apply the direct-segment procedure to obtain the result.
For Venus, apply the direct-segment procedure to obtain the result.
內金星 names Venus (金星); Mercury is 水星. The idiomatic wrongly says Mercury, and replacing with Venus matches the Chinese.
For Mercury, enter by the direct-segment procedure — that yields what is sought.
For Venus, enter by the direct-segment procedure — that yields what is sought.
Same unit: 金星 is Venus, not Mercury; the literal must make the same correction as the idiomatic.
Name as before to obtain the day and double-hour.
Add and name as before to obtain the day and double-hour.
如前加命 includes the verb 加; the idiomatic 'Name as before' omits that step, and 'Add and name as before' restores it.
Name as before to obtain fixed appearance and occultation day and double-hour.
Add and name as before to obtain fixed appearance and occultation day and double-hour.
加命如前 likewise requires 加; the idiomatic omission is a real error, and the proposed wording restores the source verb.
For Mercury, when evening-swift falls from the start of Great Heat qi through day nine and thirty-five parts of Lesser Snow qi, it is invisible;
For Mercury, when evening-swift falls from the start of Great Heat qi through day nine and thirty-five parts of Start of Winter qi, it is invisible;
立冬 is Start of Winter; 小雪 is Lesser Snow. The idiomatic wrongly names Lesser Snow, and Start of Winter restores the correct solar term.
For Mercury, when evening-swift falls from Great Heat qi initial day through Lesser Snow qi day nine and thirty-five parts and below, it is not seen;
For Mercury, when evening-swift falls from Great Heat qi initial day through Start of Winter qi day nine and thirty-five parts and below, it is not seen;
Same 立冬 misread as Lesser Snow in the literal; Start of Winter is the accurate term.
We request that a armillary-heaven sphere be made anew."
We request that an armillary-heaven sphere be made anew."
The literal 'a armillary' is ungrammatical English before a vowel sound; 'an armillary' is the required article fix and does not alter Chinese meaning.

Earlier scholars sometimes identified the entire Jiji-Yuheng with the armillary sphere, or called a globe with Ji but no Heng a celestial model, or took the sighting tube of the armillary instrument for the Heng — all of which is mistaken.

Earlier scholars sometimes identified the entire Ji-Yuheng with the armillary sphere, or called a globe with Ji but no Heng a celestial model, or took the sighting tube of the armillary instrument for the Heng — all of which is mistaken.
璣衡 is Ji plus Heng; 'Jiji' wrongly doubles the 璣 syllable. Replacing with Ji-Yuheng corrects the name without changing the rest of the sentence.
People of old sometimes called the Jiji and Yuheng the armillary sphere, or called a device with Ji but no Heng the celestial globe, or called the armillary sighting tube the Heng — all are wrong.
People of old sometimes called the Ji and Yuheng the armillary sphere, or called a device with Ji but no Heng the celestial globe, or called the armillary sighting tube the Heng — all are wrong.
Same 璣衡 reading: literal 'Jiji and Yuheng' must become 'Ji and Yuheng'.
Some did not even know what sort of instrument the Jiji and Yuheng were meant to be.
Some did not even know what sort of instrument the Ji and Yuheng were meant to be.
s0307 again has 璣衡; idiomatic 'Jiji and Yuheng' is the same doubled-syllable error and is correctly fixed to Ji and Yuheng.
In the extreme case they did not even know what instrument the Jiji and Yuheng were.
In the extreme case they did not even know what instrument the Ji and Yuheng were.
Literal of the same unit must likewise drop the spurious second 'ji' in 'Jiji'.
An edict established the Bureau for Discussing and Manufacturing the Jiji and Yuheng, placed Fu in overall charge, and made the inner attendant Liang Shicheng his deputy.
An edict established the Bureau for Discussing and Manufacturing the Ji and Yuheng, placed Fu in overall charge, and made the inner attendant Liang Shicheng his deputy.
Bureau name 討論製造璣衡所 uses 璣衡; idiomatic 'Jiji' is wrong, and 'Ji and Yuheng' matches the Chinese and the already-correct claim labels.
An edict named the office the Bureau for Discussing and Manufacturing the Jiji and Yuheng, appointed Fu to direct it overall, and the inner attendant Liang Shicheng as his deputy.
An edict named the office the Bureau for Discussing and Manufacturing the Ji and Yuheng, appointed Fu to direct it overall, and the inner attendant Liang Shicheng as his deputy.
Same bureau name in the literal: replace 'Jiji' with 'Ji' so 璣衡 is rendered once.
